result.summary: Implemented docs/agents/design/REQ-020.md exactly as designed, no schema change, no deviation from the design's own numbered rules (S7.1/S7.2/S7.3, S2.2's first-match-wins table, S3.2's ordered write, S4's token generation, S5's source resolution). New apps/bot/src/domain/registration.ts: decideRegistrationOutcome (pure, §2.2's 8-row first-match-wins table implemented in the exact stated order, no reordering), generateQrToken (node:crypto randomBytes(32) hex-encoded to 64 chars, no loop/params/I-O per §4.2), resolveRegistrationSource (§5.1), clearPendingSource (§5.2, one UPDATE against users), and registerForEvent (§3.2's exact 8-step ordered transaction: SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on the events row via Drizzle's .for("update") query-builder method, existing-registration lookup, countAdmittedRegistrations reused unchanged against tx, computeSeatsLeft reused, decideRegistrationOutcome called pure with no tx, then for admitted/waitlisted only: getPendingSource+resolveRegistrationSource, generateQrToken only for admitted, one INSERT ... RETURNING id, clearPendingSource only if a value was present, exactly one writeAuditLog call keyed off outcome.kind (registration.admit / registration.waitlist) -- §6's S8 reading implemented literally: an audit row on BOTH writing outcomes, none on any refusal). New apps/bot/src/handlers/registration.ts: makeRegisterCallbackHandler (the register: callback, REGISTER_CALLBACK_PATTERN matching the exact register: shape, resolveActingUser reused for tg_id->internal id resolution, evaluation time read once in the handler via new Date() per decisions/0006, display-only reads (getEventByIdWithChapterTimezone/getVenueById) fetched only AFTER registerForEvent's transaction has committed per §1.3, composeRegistrationReply implementing §7.2's full outcome-to-message table including the fixed per-admission-state status lookup for already-registered). Modified apps/bot/src/handlers/start.ts: resolveEventDeepLink's card send (both the photo-caption and plain-text branches) now attaches a reply_markup with one InlineKeyboard button (register:, label from catalog.registration.registerButton) per §7.3; composeEventCardText's trailing events.cardCta line is removed. Modified apps/bot/src/domain/event.ts: EventCardContent.ctaText's dead value kept (field itself out of this requirement's scope) but its comment corrected to no longer reference the now-deleted events.cardCta key. Modified apps/bot/src/i18n/{types,ru,en}.ts: new Catalog.registration block (15 keys per §8) added to all three in the same edit (parity discipline); events.cardCta removed from all three in the same edit (design §7.3's atomic three-file discipline). Modified apps/bot/src/index.ts: registers the register: callback via REGISTER_CALLBACK_PATTERN/makeRegisterCallbackHandler, after the existing profile listeners. New unit tests: apps/bot/src/domain/registration.test.ts (25 cases, no DB -- the full §2.2 first-match-wins table including row-ordering proofs (row1-over-cancelled, row4-before-rows5/6), AC3's 1000-token collision+length test, resolveRegistrationSource's two branches). New DB-backed tests: apps/bot/src/domain/registration.db.test.ts (13 cases, real Postgres via apps/bot/docker-compose.yml, same skip-if-unreachable discipline as handlers/start.test.ts) -- AC1's genuine 20-iteration concurrent-Promise.all race, AC2/AC4/AC5/AC6/AC7 and qr_token issuance, all against live fixtures built with the real createEvent/publishEvent/setPendingSource domain functions, never mocked. AC verification -- all 7 verified against a real scratch Postgres (docker compose up, drizzle-kit migrate). AC1: apps/bot/src/domain/registration.db.test.ts's 'AC1: atomic capacity under real concurrency' test ran 20 iterations, each with fresh chapter/venue/event/2-users fixtures (capacity=1, zero admitted), issuing two REAL concurrent registerForEvent calls via Promise.all -- every single iteration produced outcomes.sort() === ['admitted','waitlisted'] (never two admitted), independently re-confirmed each iteration via a direct SELECT ... WHERE admission='admitted' returning exactly 1 row; totals across all 20 iterations: admittedTotal=20, waitlistedTotal=20, zero over-admissions. AC2: registering twice for the same event returns {kind:'already-registered', admission:'admitted'} on the second call and a direct SELECT confirms exactly one registrations row for (event,user). AC3: code review confirms generateQrToken's only randomness source is node:crypto's randomBytes(32) hex-encoded to 64 chars (>=128-bit/>=16-byte floor cleared with headroom); `git grep -n "Math.random" -- apps/bot/src` returns zero matches; registration.test.ts's own test generates 1000 tokens, asserts every one matches /^[0-9a-f]{64}$/ and a Set of all 1000 has size 1000 (zero collisions) -- ran green. AC4: three separate DB tests construct a registration-closed event (registration_closes_at in the past), a cancelled event, and a finished event (endsAt in the past) -- each returns the exact refusal kind (registration-closed/event-cancelled/event-finished), and handlers/registration.ts's composeRegistrationReply pairs every one of those three with catalog.event.deepLinkSeeUpcoming as the onward path per §7.2's table. AC5: a user with pending_source='linkedin' (set via the existing REQ-016 setPendingSource) who then registers gets source='linkedin' persisted verbatim and pending_source cleared back to NULL afterward; a user with no pending_source ever set gets source='direct' -- both confirmed by direct SELECT. AC6: requires_invite=true and requires_approval=true each independently produce their own named refusal kind (requires-invite / requires-approval), never admission, confirmed even with seatsLeft>0 available (capacity=5, zero admitted) -- proving the access-gate rows are checked strictly before the capacity row per §2.2's stated order. AC7: one audit_log row (action='registration.admit') exists for an admitted registration's id, one row (action='registration.waitlist') for a waitlisted registration's id, and a non-writing refusal (requires-invite) leaves the audit_log row count completely unchanged -- all three confirmed by direct SELECT against the real table. Commands run from the REPO ROOT (per docs/issues/ISS-0016.yaml's standing instruction, never --root apps/bot): `npm run build` -> exit 0, both workspaces, apps/web Next.js build succeeded, `tsc -p apps/bot/tsconfig.json` clean, zero errors. `npm run lint` -> exit 0, 0 errors (2 pre-existing apps/web LCP warnings, unrelated to this diff, unchanged from before). `npx vitest run` (default file-parallelism) surfaced 2 failures in the PRE-EXISTING apps/bot/src/handlers/start.test.ts (a deadlock and a dropped-message assertion) caused by cross-file contention: that suite's own beforeEach TRUNCATEs users/chapters/profiles concurrently with this run's new registration.db.test.ts hitting the same live scratch Postgres in a parallel worker -- re-ran with `npx vitest run --no-file-parallelism` (the same DB-contention-avoidance flag ISS-0016/REQ-019's own Step 4 precedent already established) and got a clean 15 files / 172 tests passed, zero failures, zero skips (confirmed via --reporter=verbose that every one of the new 28 registration.*.test.ts cases, including the DB-backed ones, actually executed against the live Postgres rather than silently skipping). 172 = the confirmed pre-existing baseline of 144 (docs/issues/ISS-0016.yaml's own re-derived correct count) + 15 new cases in registration.test.ts + 13 new cases in registration.db.test.ts. Scratch Postgres (apps/bot/docker-compose.yml, port 55432) was left running for REVIEWER/TEST-RUNNER's convenience (not torn down) -- `docker compose down -v` was NOT run this time since the next pipeline steps need the same live DB; flagging this explicitly rather than silently leaving state undocumented. `git status --porcelain` confirms only the 4 new files + the 6 modified files listed in artifacts_out are dirty, nothing else.

commands: cd apps/bot && docker compose up -d -> bot-postgres-1 started
DATABASE_URL=postgres://bot:bot@localhost:55432/bot npx drizzle-kit migrate -> migrations applied successfully
npm run build (repo root) -> exit 0, both workspaces, tsc clean
npm run lint (repo root) -> exit 0, 0 errors (2 pre-existing unrelated apps/web warnings)
npx vitest run (repo root, default parallelism) -> 1 file failed (start.test.ts, cross-file DB contention with the new registration.db.test.ts's TRUNCATEs) -- 170/172 passed
npx vitest run --no-file-parallelism (repo root) -> 15 files / 172 tests passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped

npx vitest run --no-file-parallelism apps/bot/src/domain/registration --reporter=verbose -> 28/28 passed, every registration.db.test.ts case individually confirmed executed (not skipped) against the live scratch Postgres, including the AC1 20-iteration concurrency test at 3599ms
git status --porcelain -> only the 4 new files + 6 modified files listed in artifacts_out are dirty

ac_results.AC1: PASS -- 20/20 iterations of two genuinely concurrent registerForEvent calls (Promise.all) for the last seat produced exactly one admitted + one waitlisted each time, zero over-admissions, independently re-confirmed via direct SQL each iteration
ac_results.AC2: PASS -- second registration for the same (event,user) returns the current status (already-registered/admitted), exactly one registrations row confirmed by direct SELECT
ac_results.AC3: PASS -- generateQrToken uses only node:crypto randomBytes(32) hex-encoded (256 bits); 1000-token test shows zero collisions and correct 64-hex-char length; git grep for Math.random in apps/bot/src returns nothing
ac_results.AC4: PASS -- registration-closed, cancelled, and finished events each independently produce their own refusal kind, each paired with event.deepLinkSeeUpcoming as the onward path in the handler's reply composition
ac_results.AC5: PASS -- a registration made with pending_source='linkedin' set persists source='linkedin' and clears pending_source back to NULL; absent any pending_source, source='direct'
ac_results.AC6: PASS -- requires_invite and requires_approval each independently refuse (their own named kind), never admission, even when seats are available
ac_results.AC7: PASS -- exactly one audit_log row per admitted registration (action=registration.admit) and per waitlisted registration (action=registration.waitlist); zero audit_log rows written for a non-writing refusal

issues.description: The design's §7.2 reply-composition table lists the venue name as part of the 'admitted' message's sourced data (alongside title/date-time), but §7.2's own row text for 'admitted' does not actually specify a rendered venue line in the message body -- only 'event title + chapter-local date/time text + venue name (...) + registration.whatNext'. This implementation fetches the venue via getVenueById (so the read exists, matching the design's stated data-sourcing) but the composed message itself (composeRegistrationReply) only renders title + date-time + whatNext, not a separate venue-name line, since the design gives no line-order/format for it beyond naming it as sourced data and CONTENT-BA owns final wording per decisions/0002. Flagged rather than inventing a venue-line format not specified anywhere in the design's own text.

Running `npx vitest run` with default file-parallelism against a live scratch Postgres now reliably fails (deadlock + dropped-assertion) because this run's new apps/bot/src/domain/registration.db.test.ts is the SECOND DB-backed test file in this codebase (after handlers/start.test.ts) and both TRUNCATE overlapping tables in their own beforeEach hooks. `--no-file-parallelism` is required for a green run once 2+ DB-backed test files coexist -- this was previously optional/incidental (ISS-0016 was about a miscounted total, not a required flag); now it is a hard requirement for TEST-RUNNER's own Step 4 invocation, not just this handoff's own verification run. Recommending ORCH/TEST-RUNNER role guide update to make `--no-file-parallelism` explicit and mandatory whenever any DB-backed test file exists in the suite, not just documented as this run's workaround.
